_README: §220c (2026-10-06, user: "yes to all 6"): series-BZ sessions that PRECEDE a series' first stored bar. update_sf_data.insert_bz_history()
splices bz_backfill.json.gz blocks only AFTER an existing bar (`after`), so a relisting that traded in BZ before its first EQ session
never landed (RAJOIL -> ROML: 17 BZ sessions 07-30 Oct 2020 missing; the series began 03-Nov-2020). build_bz_backfill.py --build rewrites
its whole ledger, so prefix blocks live HERE, hand-built from NSE's own daily bhavcopies with the provenance below.
Block: before = the series' first stored bar it attaches in front of; anchorRaw = NSE's raw close on `before`; expectedScale = stored/raw close on
`before` (explained by scaleWhy); bars = RAW NSE rows (see barsFormat); at apply time f = stored close on `before` / anchorRaw puts them on the series' CURRENT

level (prices x f, 4 dp / 6 below Rs 1; t = turnover lakhs 1 dp; v raw; dv 100 = trade-for-trade) — nothing pre-scaled, the bar_inserts.json rule. Controls: each bar's PREV_CLOSE = the previous bar's close; the last raw close = NSE's
PREV_CLOSE on `before`. Applied by update_sf_data.insert_bz_prefix() — idempotent (a block whose first bar is present is skipped); a block whose f differs from expectedScale by >0.5% is
reported and left out (the series was re-anchored in a way nobody has checked against this block).

ROML.scaleWhy: scripts/rights_terp.json [ROML, 20230209, 0.656, 0.7707]: the Feb-2023 rights TERP puts every bar before 2023-02-09 at x0.656; the live store's 2020-11-03 close 4.9856 = NSE 7.60 x 0.656
